newsitem.title: USA: U.S. 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates rise 2 basis points.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates rise 2 basis points.

text.p: Average commitment rates on U.S. 30- and 15-year fixed-rate mortgages inched up in the week to May 30 from the prior week, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
Thirty-year mortgages increased to an average 7.94 percent from 7.92 percent last week, while 15-year mortgages rose to 7.47 percent from 7.45 percent.
One-year adjustable rate mortgages rose three basis points to 5.83 percent from 5.80 percent last week, Freddie Mac said.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 8.03 percent, the 15-year 7.54 percent and the ARM 5.76 percent.
Freddie Mac said it expected rates to hold steady in the near future.
"The 30-year mortgage rate is still under 8 percent with no signs of any dramatic changes in store," Robert Van Order, chief economist for Freddie Mac, said in a statement.

The Commerce Department announced Wednesday that new orders for costly manufactured goods rose in April after a March slump, although declining order backlogs suggested slower industrial activity ahead.
The government will release its preliminary estimate of the first quarter Gross Domestic Product, first quarter corporate profits and single family home figures on Friday.

Lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.7 percent on 15-year mortgages, up from an average 1.6 percent charged last week, and 1.5 percent on ARM loans, unchanged from the previous week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
